metadata.title: Infinigen Primitive API Reference
metadata.description: Facade-focused DSL summary for primitive-driven programs. Keep the prompt surface on axis-aligned primitive composition helpers (cuboids, triangular prisms, half-cylinders) instead of the broader curve/modifier stack.

replay_context: Facade primitives in this family are bbox-first and assemble geometry by placing axis-aligned primitives.
Use direct primitive composition helpers (`new_bbox`, `new_tri_prism`, `new_half_cylinder`) before considering broader Infinigen curve or modifier APIs.
script_notes: Prefer `new_bbox(...)` for walls, windows, lintels, sills, jambs, and other rectangular panel-like elements.
Use `new_tri_prism(...)` for gables, pediments, awnings, and any isoceles triangular profile that extrudes through a third axis.
Use `new_half_cylinder(...)` for arched window heads, half-round dormers, barrel-vault details, and any half-disk profile that extrudes through a third axis.

All three primitive helpers share the same coordinate convention: arguments are flat scalars (no tuples), the base/diameter segment must be axis-aligned, and the extrusion (thickness) axis is auto-derived from the remaining axis.
Use `join_objects(...)` only when the primitive script needs one merged object after constructing multiple primitive pieces.
imports: from infinigen.assets.utils.object import join_objects, new_bbox, new_tri_prism, new_half_cylinder

functions.name: new_bbox
functions.signature: new_bbox(xmin: float, xmax: float, ymin: float, ymax: float, zmin: float, zmax: float)
functions.purpose: Create one axis-aligned cuboid from explicit min/max bounds. This is the primary facade-building primitive.
functions.returns: bpy.types.Object (MESH) for the cuboid, linked to the active scene.
side_effects: Applies the transform so the mesh matches the requested bbox
functions.notes: Use this directly for facade panels and openings. Do not replace it with unrelated curve helpers.

functions.name: new_tri_prism
functions.signature: new_tri_prism(x0: float, y0: float, z0: float, x1: float, y1: float, z1: float, height: float, thickness: float, rise_x: float = 0, rise_y: float = 0, rise_z: float = 1)
functions.purpose: Create one isoceles triangular prism (gable, pediment, awning, etc.) from a flat axis-aligned base segment, an apex offset, and an extrusion thickness.

inputs.name: x0, y0, z0
inputs.description: Start point of the base segment (one corner of the triangle base).

inputs.name: x1, y1, z1
inputs.description: End point of the base segment (other corner of the triangle base). The base must be axis-aligned: exactly one of (x1-x0, y1-y0, z1-z0) is nonzero.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Distance from the base midpoint to the apex along the rise direction.

inputs.name: thickness
inputs.description: Extrusion length along the third (auto-derived) axis. Positive extrudes in +axis, negative in -axis.

inputs.name: rise_x, rise_y, rise_z
inputs.description: Apex rise direction. Must be axis-aligned with exactly one nonzero component (sign sets the direction); must be perpendicular to the base axis. Default (0, 0, 1) puts the apex straight up along +Z.

functions.returns: bpy.types.Object (MESH) for the triangular prism, linked to the active collection.
side_effects: Creates a new mesh object with 6 vertices and 5 faces (2 triangle caps + base quad + 2 slope quads)
functions.notes: The third axis (thickness extrusion) is auto-derived as the axis that is neither the base axis nor the rise axis, so the user never has to name it. For a vertical front-facing gable on a building, use the default rise (apex up Z) and set the base segment along X; thickness then runs through Y.

functions.name: new_half_cylinder
functions.signature: new_half_cylinder(x0: float, y0: float, z0: float, x1: float, y1: float, z1: float, height: float, thickness: float, rise_x: float = 0, rise_y: float = 0, rise_z: float = 1, segments: int = 16)
functions.purpose: Create one half-elliptical-cylinder prism (arched window head, half-round dormer, segmental arch, barrel-vault detail) from a flat axis-aligned diameter segment, an arc rise, and an extrusion thickness.

inputs.name: x0, y0, z0
inputs.description: Start point of the flat diameter (one end of the half-disk's straight edge).

inputs.name: x1, y1, z1
inputs.description: End point of the flat diameter. The diameter must be axis-aligned: exactly one of (x1-x0, y1-y0, z1-z0) is nonzero.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Arc rise above the diameter, along the rise direction. Equals base_length/2 for a true semicircle, smaller for a squat/segmental arch, larger for a tall stilted ellipse.

inputs.name: thickness
inputs.description: Extrusion length along the third (auto-derived) axis. Positive extrudes in +axis, negative in -axis.

inputs.name: rise_x, rise_y, rise_z
inputs.description: Direction the arc bulges. Must be axis-aligned with exactly one nonzero component (sign sets the direction); must be perpendicular to the base axis. Default (0, 0, 1) makes the arc bulge straight up along +Z.

inputs.name: segments
inputs.description: Number of edges spanning the half-ellipse. Default 16 is smooth at typical facade scale; increase for closeups, decrease for distant LODs.

functions.returns: bpy.types.Object (MESH) for the half-cylinder prism, linked to the active collection.
side_effects: Creates a new mesh object with 2 * (segments + 1) vertices and (segments + 1 + 2) faces (2 half-disk caps + curved side strip + flat bottom)
functions.notes: The arc is a half-ellipse: horizontal semi-axis = base_length / 2, vertical semi-axis = height. Pass height = base_length / 2 to recover the perfect semicircle. The third axis (thickness extrusion) is auto-derived as the axis that is neither the base axis nor the rise axis. For an arched window head on a vertical wall, set the base segment along X at the desired window-top Z, leave rise default (+Z), and thickness then runs through Y.

functions.name: join_objects
functions.purpose: Merge several primitive-built pieces into one object when the primitive script needs a combined facade element.

inputs.name: objs
inputs.description: Objects to merge into the active object.

side_effects: Merges object data into one output object
functions.notes: Use only after constructing the individual primitives that belong together.

examples.description: Create one facade opening surround from explicit bounds
Add a vertical gable above the front wall (base along X at z=6, apex up Z, depth Y)
Add a side-wall awning with apex pointing in +X (base along Y, depth through Z)
examples.code: awning = new_tri_prism(2.0, 1.0, 3.0, 2.0, 3.0, 3.0, height=0.6, thickness=0.1, rise_x=1, rise_y=0, rise_z=0)

examples.description: Add a true semicircular arch over a window (height = base_length / 2 = 0.6)
Add a squat segmental arch (rise smaller than half the diameter)
Add an arched dormer on a side wall (diameter along Y, dome up Z, depth +X)
examples.code: dormer = new_half_cylinder(5.0, 1.0, 4.0, 5.0, 2.5, 4.0, height=0.6, thickness=0.4, rise_z=1, segments=20)

examples.description: Merge several facade strips into one wall-border object
